## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Rebase and review status

Current head: `a92514131a2944b744a1bf512972f9a972fed83b`. The stack is rebased onto fetched upstream main
`73c4ebdac57de0d89bb20d5dfabed340449c8b0d`; commit prefixes now match the four PR titles.
The latest `pr-review` skill and checklist were read from this rebased checkout.

The rebase updates the `PrecisionConfig` parallelize contract, checks QSA
accelerator capture before dynamic metadata construction, preserves Flash-Next's
BF16 GDN parameter policy, restores the PP test imports, and retains upstream's
redundant-test deletions. Current exact-prefix checks: all-file pre-commit passes
and 50 CPU tests pass. The full-stack CPU run hides GPUs so the
upstream CPU FSDP test does not select the unavailable FA4 package.

[Claude's review of #5782](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782#pullrequestreview-5761648327)
still has open FSDP/indexer and QSA training-memory findings. Earlier local
approval claims are withdrawn. HF/GPU/convergence results below are historical
captures at their stated SHAs; this rebase has not received fresh GPU validation.
The human summary placeholder is retained for the author to complete before review.

Planned next revision:

1. Connect a finite zero indexer gradient on empty/short-document ranks and define frozen-indexer behavior when no KL objective is configured.
2. Reuse compatible Attention Gym selection, qualify public efficient SDPA and per-query-chunk remat, and measure saved forward/backward memory. Existing [#678](https://github.com/meta-pytorch/attention-gym/pull/678)/[#679](https://github.com/meta-pytorch/attention-gym/pull/679) lack the complete grouped separate-K/V backward path.
3. Simplify the norm/head-count plumbing, adapter handling, checkpoint fixture and parity harness; retain behavioral tests and clarify table-memory/reset semantics.
4. Validate the resulting stack on the requested DCT GB300 tenant before asking for re-review.

## Why

TorchTitan cannot build or train the released Flash-Next architecture. Qwen3.5
already supplies its GDN, gated shared experts, multimodal preprocessing,
vision encoder, FSDP and optimizer hooks, but the decoder has different residual,
lexical and sparse-attention computation. This PR adds those differences using
the existing model lifecycle and component configs.

Component reuse needs public Qwen3.5 config factories, ordinary `Linear.Config`
router gates, and a shared structural annotation contract for QSA metadata.
This model supplies the concrete consumer of all three shared API changes.

For a packed document with T tokens and hidden width D, a decoder block carries
four streams instead of one:

```text
[T, 4*D] -> PLE lookup/injection -> gated read [T, D]
          -> GDN or selected QSA -> gated residual write [T, 4*D]
          -> gated read [T, D] -> shared routed MoE -> gated write [T, 4*D]
```

Original token IDs and document positions reach PLE independently of multimodal
rotary coordinates. Masked/padded tokens do not contribute to MoE auxiliary
counts. The optional indexer-teacher objective trains only the indexer.

## What changed

- Expose `make_qwen35_deltanet_config` and `make_qwen35_vision_encoder_config`,
  accept the shared `Linear.Config` router-gate base, and use structural
  attention metadata annotation. Factory-callsite renames are mechanical;
  shared arithmetic and parameter layouts are unchanged.
- Add model-specific gated residual, offset/gated normalization, partial MRoPE,
  n-gram PLE, rounded router scoring and chunked selected-token QSA reference code.
- Reuse Qwen3.5's GDN/vision config factories and training/FSDP lifecycle.
- Export the standard model/flavor/build API and explicit indexer-loss config.
- Add strict HF mappings for all 1,627 released decoder/vision keys, including
  numeric lexical shard ordering; the 31 MTP keys are outside this model.
- Add independent feature/backward tests and the same-weight HF parity harness.

This initial increment supports FSDP. TP/SP and EP follow in `2/n`, the shared
deterministic GDN policy in `3/n`, and PP in `4/n`. CP remains unsupported.

## User-facing changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Qwen config factories are private and shared gate typing excludes ordinary `Linear` | Public factories, the shared `Linear.Config` base and structural metadata annotation support the new model |
| Flash-Next has no model/flavor factory | `build_model_config("debugmodel", seq_len=64, parallelism=ParallelismConfig())` builds the reduced decoder; the released flavor is available for meta construction |
| Flash-Next checkpoint has no TorchTitan adapter | The native/HF adapter maps the released decoder and vision tensors and excludes unsupported MTP |
| Flash-Next image/video tokens have no training path | The inherited Qwen3.5 processor and vision encoder fuse features into the model's placeholder positions |

## Numerics

The shared API refactor changes no arithmetic or tensor layouts. Its preserved
Qwen3.5 MoE video comparison uses actual base `01586df70d7599d59a87663f39670a8c694924c3`
and head `06cd1fb1c4e1b340f5398c5b4ed1459530589d64`: ten steps on one GB300,
seed 42 and strict deterministic execution. All 20 full-precision loss/grad_norm
values agree bitwise; loss goes from 13.087042808532715 to 0.34375783801078796.
This historical comparison covers the original shared API refactor; later upstream dtype changes were outside that capture.

Pinned checkpoint `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` revision
`de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540`; Transformers revision
`494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab`.

The reduced eight-layer model retains both GDN/QSA, all four streams, PLE,
and routed/shared experts. Its 39-token text fixture exercises real pruning.
CPU FP32 and BF16 train/eval comparisons pass: full logits, normalized CE,
embedding-input gradients and all 184 mapped decoder parameter gradients.
Full image/video fusion, MRoPE and masked CE additionally compare both pixel
input gradients and all 225 decoder/vision parameter gradients. Standalone
vision compares all 41 parameter gradients.

On the previously reviewed prefix `b9bdfa4da3ca1708359834cad53027abca181272`, the CPU
FP32/BF16 and CUDA BF16 harnesses all pass. The CUDA multimodal comparison has
CE 4.157130241394043 versus HF 4.157289981842041 and maximum logit difference
0.00390625. Both pixel inputs have nonzero gradients, and all 225 mapped
parameter gradients pass their original RMS/infinity bounds.

BF16 multimodal routing uses ordinary seeded projections because near-tied
expert cutoffs amplified the shared fused GDN's BF16 rounding. The recorded
seeds are 30003/31002/32004/33011/34001/35007/36023/37036. All 128 query/layer
cutoffs match naturally and exceed a preregistered margin: four times both
actual raw-logit drift and dtype epsilon times logit scale, with a 0.002 floor.
The minimum observed margin ratio is 1.0463576. Primary text, standalone vision
and FP32 multimodal weights are unchanged; no routes or scores are imposed.

Real FSDP2 uses the same FP32 checkpoint and global 512-token batch as the
baseline. All 190 preclip reconstructed parameter gradients pass the original
bounds; maximum absolute difference is 3.725290298461914e-09. This was captured
at `a1e1d506c`; subsequent port amendments changed the reference fixture and
README, then migrated two recipe settings to upstream's configurable
TensorBoard logger API. The model computation and sharding are unchanged.
No fitted gradient scaling is applied.

The reference results above identify their actual capture revisions. The current
base and exact-head CPU/lint results are recorded separately above. New GPU
qualification is part of the revision plan.

| Training check | GPUs / steps | Full-precision result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C4, reduced eight-layer decoder, sequence 256, official tokenizer/vocabulary | 1 GB300 / 100 | Loss 12.553109169006348 -> 7.390992164611816; first/last ten means 12.4797701836 -> 7.9403163433 |
| Actual image/video debug training recipe | 1 GB300 / 10 | Loss 7.678964614868164 -> 3.388758420944214 |

Both training checks use seed 42 and strict deterministic execution. C4 retains
the reduced PLE table and uses vocabulary 248320 and EOS 248044 with streamed
`allenai/c4`, English training split. Its loss and gradient norm at all 100
steps are also bitwise identical before/after the padding-mask callsite cleanup.

## Testing

Current rebased prefix: `a92514131a2944b744a1bf512972f9a972fed83b`. Its all-file pre-commit hooks and
50 CPU config/feature cases pass. Numerical captures below retain
their original source references.

- Exact-prefix `pre-commit run --all-files`: all hooks pass.
- Exact-prefix CPU feature/config tests: 50 pass.
- Audited every shared factory caller, router config subclass and metadata
  runtime check; the same 50-case prefix includes the shared build/config tests.
- FP32/BF16 CPU HF harness with 39 tokens and full multimodal backward: pass.
- CUDA BF16 HF harness with 39 tokens and full multimodal backward: pass.
- Real FSDP2 checkpoint/batch/preclip-gradient comparison: pass.
- C4 convergence (100 steps) and image/video training (10 steps): pass.
- Claude's FSDP/indexer and QSA saved-memory must-fix findings remain open; the earlier local approval claim is withdrawn.

```bash
pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_qwen3_8_flash_next.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_build_model_config.py -q
python -m scripts.checkpoint_conversion.numerical_tests_qwen3_8_flash_next \
  --device cuda --backbone-dtype bfloat16 --full-token-count 39
NGPU=1 MODULE=torchtitan_recipes.tests.models.qwen3_8_flash_next \
  CONFIG=qwen38_flash_next_debugmodel_mm ./run_train.sh
```

## Alternatives considered

- Reimplement shared GDN/vision or add model-specific flags to common modules:
  rejected because the public Qwen3.5 config factories already supply both.
- Full dense attention with a sparse mask: the selected-token implementation
  expresses the released block/tail semantics directly, but its saved training
  memory is unresolved and requires the revision described above.

Full released-checkpoint materialization, 51.2B-table distributed conversion,
full-size training, inference KV caching and MTP are outside the validated scope.
The SDPA MATH path retains activations across query chunks; full-scale memory
and throughput are unqualified.

## Stack

This stack supersedes [the earlier all-in-one draft #5655](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5655).
Its original branch and worktree are retained for reference.

Draft 1/n of the Flash-Next implementation.

- [1/n Add Flash-Next model, FSDP and checkpoint reference coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782)
- [2/n Add tensor and expert parallelism with batched QSA teachers](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5783)
- [3/n Honor deterministic GDN normalization](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5784)
- [4/n Add pipeline stages, remat and numerical integration coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5785)

This combined model increment includes the shared API changes from #5781
and targets `main`. Merge the stack in order.

nodes.body:
**Claude finished @shuhuayu's task in 3m 13s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/41748422637)

---
**Request changes** -- see the [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782#pullrequestreview) (indexer grads can be `None` on some ranks under FSDP; the QSA reference path doesn't scale).

**Verdict: Request changes** -- under FSDP the QSA indexer can end up with `None` grads on some ranks, and the QSA training path's saved activations grow with sequence length times the 2,048-token budget. An attention-gym path for the same pattern already exists in `deepseek_v4`.

**What this PR does.** Adds `torchtitan/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/`, built on `Qwen35Model`. The model has a four-stream gated residual, a hashed n-gram PLE in layer 1, and QSA every fourth layer (the other layers are Qwen3.5 GDN). QSA is an indexer that picks top-k complete 4-token blocks, plus selected-token SDPA and an optional indexer KL loss. The PR also makes two Qwen3.5 config factories public, widens the shared router gate type to `Linear.Config`, and turns `AttentionMetadata` into a Protocol. FSDP only; TP, EP, PP and CP raise.

**Example.** `build_model_config("debugmodel", seq_len=64, parallelism=ParallelismConfig())` builds 8 layers, with QSA at `layer_id` 3 and 7 and GDN elsewhere. Activations go `[T, 256] -> repeat -> [T, 1024]`. In each block, a gated read gives `[T, 256]`, then attention or MoE, then a gated write back to `[T, 1024]`. With `token_budget=16`, a QSA query at position 38 of one document attends to the 4 best complete earlier blocks (16 tokens) plus its own incomplete tail of up to 3 tokens. Each attended token is gathered per query, then attended with SDPA MATH.

### Must fix
1. **PR description.** "Summary (human-written)" is empty. Also, the title says "1/n Add Flash-Next model", but commit e0aceb3 is "2/n Add Flash-Next model" and the body says "TP/SP and EP follow in 2/n".
2. **Design: the QSA training path doesn't scale** (`attention.py:182-209`, `:282-320`). It is a Python loop over 16-query chunks that gathers K/V per query and runs SDPA MATH. The saved activations are about 4 MB per token per QSA layer at the released settings, plus an O(T^2) indexer score term (inline comment). `deepseek_v4/compressor.py` and `deepseek_v4/attention.py` already do indexer top-k, gathered sparse attention and KL distillation on attn_gym's `lightning_indexer` / `gather_attn` (meta-pytorch, allowed by core principle 3). Please say whether those kernels can express QSA (4-token blocks plus tail, 2 KV heads). If they can, use them. If not, add a TODO with an attention-gym issue link, and state in the README which sequence lengths are trainable.
3. `attention.py:281-299` -- indexer `grad=None` on ranks with no complete block, so FSDP2 reduce-scatters may not match (inline comment, with a one-line fix).

### Should consider
- `attention.py:236` -- `QSAInnerAttention.Config.num_heads` cancels in `block_kl`; delete it.
- `norm.py:56` -- renamed kwargs force rewriting the sharding config in `flavors.py:410-416`, and the override drops `@local_compile`.
- `state_dict_adapter.py:120` -- the MTP warning never fires on the DCP path; drop the keys explicitly instead.
- `test_qwen3_8_flash_next.py:488` -- the shard-order test can't catch the sort bug it is named for. The file also belongs in a `qwen3_8_flash_next/` test folder.
- `numerical_tests_qwen3_8_flash_next.py:182` -- imports private GPU-test helpers and monkeypatches production code.
- `tests/assets/qwen3_8_flash_next/checkpoint_schema.json` (1,635 lines) has one consumer, and no other model keeps such an asset. Replace it with a compact check: key count, one GDN-layer and one QSA-layer key pattern, the shard count, and a hash of the sorted names.
- `embedding.py:67,78` -- the "feature-sharded" docstrings are inaccurate: `NGramTable` is replicated over TP and all-gathered whole by FSDP. For `125B-A6B` that means all-gathering a 51.2B-parameter table in both forward and backward. Either reject that flavor for training or document it.
- Tests that don't earn their cost:
  - `test_router_bfloat16_ties_mixing_and_backward[compiled]` exercises a path no recipe enables.
  - `test_packed_padding_is_excluded_from_moe_auxiliary_gradients` mostly duplicates `common/test_moe.py`, and it swaps out the configured `batch_wise` loss.
  - `test_deltanet_uses_sigmoid_output_gate` runs in FP32 with ones-initialized weights, so it can't tell `InputDtypeGatedRMSNorm` apart from the base class.
- `torchtitan_recipes/tests/models/qwen3_8_flash_next.py:49` -- `qwen38_flash_next_debugmodel_ac` has no consumer.

### Questions
- With `indexer_loss=None` (the default), the indexer never gets a gradient, so training from scratch keeps it at random init. Is that intended? If only fine-tuning is supported in that mode, should training with `indexer_loss=None` raise?
- N-gram hashing resets history at EOS and at `positions == 0`, but the PLE conv and QSA visibility reset only at `positions == 0`. Does that match the reference?

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **Shared changes.** These look fine. `HiMidLoLinear` subclasses `Linear`, so every existing router config still type-checks, and no `isinstance` check depends on the `AttentionMetadata` union. The `qwen3_5/flavors.py` renames are mechanical.
- **FSDP2 grad handling.** `post_backward` collects only params whose `unsharded_param.grad is not None`. So a rank with zero complete blocks in its microbatch sends a smaller reduce-scatter for that block's FSDP unit.
- **Memory arithmetic** (released config). Per query, the gathered K is 2 KV heads x 2051 tokens x 256 dims x 2 bytes = 2.1 MB, and V is the same. That is about 4.2 MB per token per QSA layer, kept for backward, before any MATH-backend GQA repeat.
- **Hidden syncs.** The `.nonzero()` calls in `QSAIndexMetadata.from_inputs` sync once per step, and `min(block_topk, block_ends_G.numel())` makes shapes data-dependent. Accelerator graphs are rejected, so this is acceptable for now, but any compiled region around the indexer would recompile every step.

</details>

Not verified: the FSDP2 desync and the memory estimates were not reproduced on GPUs. Whether `gather_attn` supports multiple KV heads is unverified.

**Indexer params can get `grad=None` on some ranks, so FSDP2 reduce-scatters may not match.** The KL is the indexer's only gradient path: its input is `x_TD.detach()` (L370) and the selected indices are integers.

When a rank's microbatch has no complete 4-token block (all padding, or every document shorter than 4 valid tokens), `num_blocks == 0`. Then `raw_sum` stays the detached `new_zeros(())`, and `index_qk_proj`, `q_layernorm` and `k_layernorm` get `grad=None` on that rank while other ranks have grads. FSDP2 only reduces params whose `grad is not None`, so the ranks would issue different reduce-scatters. The `all_padding` unit test runs in one process and can't catch this.

Smallest fix: seed the sum from the graph, so the inject always carries a (zero) indexer gradient.
```python
raw_sum = scores_TB.sum() * 0  # keep indexer params in the graph on every rank
```
I haven't reproduced this on multiple GPUs.

**Saved activations here grow as T x J, not with the chunk size.** Each 16-query chunk gathers `keys_QHJK` and `values_QHJV` with J = 2048 + 3, 2 KV heads and head dim 256. MATH SDPA keeps these inputs for backward. At the released settings that is about 2 MB per token each for K and V, so roughly 17 GB per QSA layer at T=4096, with 12 QSA layers. That is before any GQA expansion inside the math backend (unverified). The indexer's `scores_QHG.relu()` adds another O(T^2) fp32 term (L184-187).

The README says gathers are "bounded by query chunks". That holds for transient memory only, not for what is saved for training. See the design item in the review body: `deepseek_v4` already runs indexer top-k plus gathered sparse attention through attn_gym's `lightning_indexer` / `gather_attn`.

+                or self.token_budget % self.compress_ratio
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "token_budget must be a positive multiple of compress_ratio"
+                )
+            if not 0 < self.rotary_dim <= self.head_dim or self.rotary_dim % 2:
+                raise ValueError("rotary_dim must be positive, even and <= head_dim")
+
+    def __init__(self, config: Config):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.num_heads = config.num_heads
+        self.head_dim = config.head_dim
+        self.rotary_dim = config.rotary_dim
+        self.compress_ratio = config.compress_ratio
+        self.block_topk = config.token_budget // config.compress_ratio
+        self.chunk_size = config.chunk_size
+        self.index_qk_proj = config.index_qk_proj.build()
+        self.q_layernorm = config.q_layernorm.build()
+        self.k_layernorm = config.k_layernorm.build()
+        self.rope = config.rope.build()
+
+    def _rotate(self, x_THK: torch.Tensor, positions_T: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        rotary_THR = x_THK[..., : self.rotary_dim]
+        rotary_THR, _ = self.rope(rotary_THR, rotary_THR, positions_T)
+        return torch.cat((rotary_THR, x_THK[..., self.rotary_dim :]), -1)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        x_TD: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        document_positions_T: torch.Tensor,
+        padding_mask_T: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        metadata: QSAIndexMetadata | None = None,
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        num_tokens = x_TD.shape[0]
+        indices_T = torch.arange(num_tokens, device=x_TD.device)
+        qk_TC = self.index_qk_proj(x_TD)
+        remat.recompute_needs_tensor(qk_TC)
+        query_TC, raw_key_TK = qk_TC.split(
+            (self.num_heads * self.head_dim, self.head_dim), -1
+        )
+        query_THK = self._rotate(
+            self.q_layernorm(query_TC.unflatten(-1, (self.num_heads, self.head_dim))),
+            positions,
+        )
+        if metadata is None:
+            metadata = QSAIndexMetadata.from_inputs(
+                document_positions_T,
+                padding_mask_T=padding_mask_T,
+                compress_ratio=self.compress_ratio,
+            )
+        starts_T, valid_T, block_indices_GR, tail_indices_TR = metadata
+        block_ends_G = block_indices_GR[:, -1]
+        pooled_GK = raw_key_TK[block_indices_GR].float().mean(1).to(raw_key_TK.dtype)
+        key_GK = self._rotate(
+            self.k_layernorm(pooled_GK).unsqueeze(1), positions[block_indices_GR[:, 0]]
+        ).squeeze(1)
+        num_selected = min(self.block_topk, block_ends_G.numel())
+        selected_indices = []
+        selected_scores = []
+        for start in range(0, num_tokens, self.chunk_size):
+            stop = start + self.chunk_size
+            scores_QHG = torch.einsum(
+                "qhk,gk->qhg", query_THK[start:stop].float(), key_GK.float()
+            )
+            scores_QG = scores_QHG.relu().sum(1) * self.head_dim**-0.5
+            visible_QG = (
+                (block_ends_G[None] <= indices_T[start:stop, None])
+                & (starts_T[block_ends_G][None] == starts_T[start:stop, None])
+                & valid_T[start:stop, None]
+            )
+            ranked_scores_QG = scores_QG.masked_fill(~visible_QG, -torch.inf)
+            # ReLU creates exact zero-score ties. Chronological tie ordering
+            # keeps past selections independent of masked future documents.
+            blocks_QB = ranked_scores_QG.argsort(dim=-1, descending=True, stable=True)[
+                :, :num_selected
+            ]
+            scores_QB = ranked_scores_QG.gather(-1, blocks_QB)
+            tokens_QBR = block_indices_GR[blocks_QB].masked_fill(
+                ~scores_QB.isfinite().unsqueeze(-1), -1
+            )
+            selected_indices.append(
+                torch.cat(
+                    (tokens_QBR.flatten(-2), tail_indices_TR[start:stop]), -1
+                ).int()
+            )
+            selected_scores.append(scores_QB)
+        return torch.cat(selected_indices), torch.cat(selected_scores)
+
+
+class QSAIndexerLoss(AuxLoss):
+    """KL loss on selected complete blocks from the report's sparse training stage."""
+
+    @dataclass(kw_only=True, slots=True)
+    class Config(AuxLoss.Config):
+        pass
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def block_kl(scores_QB: torch.Tensor, teacher_QB: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        valid_QB = scores_QB.isfinite()
+        log_probs_QB = F.log_softmax(
+            scores_QB.masked_fill(~valid_QB, torch.finfo(torch.float32).min), -1
+        )
+        teacher_QB = teacher_QB.detach() * valid_QB
+        teacher_QB = teacher_QB / teacher_QB.sum(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-30)
+        return (torch.xlogy(teacher_QB, teacher_QB) - teacher_QB * log_probs_QB).sum()
+
+
+class QSAInnerAttention(InnerAttention):
+    """Selected-token SDPA with bounded gathers and a detached attention teacher."""
+
+    @dataclass(kw_only=True, slots=True)
+    class Config(InnerAttention.Config):
+        compress_ratio: int
+        num_heads: int

The override renames the base kwargs `input`/`gate` to `input_THD`/`gate_THD`. That rename is the only reason `flavors.py:410-416` has to copy and rewrite `gated_rms_norm_sharding_config()` keys behind an `assert`. The override also drops the base class's `@local_compile("gated_rmsnorm", batch_invariant=False)`.

Keep the parent's parameter names and the decorator, then pass `gated_rms_norm_sharding_config()` unchanged in flavors. That removes about 6 lines.

This warning never fires on the HF load path. DCP calls `to_hf`, loads only those keys, then calls `from_hf`, so `mtp.*` never arrives here. In offline conversion the keys are actually dropped by the parent's silent `continue` on unmapped keys.

nodes.body:
The name says "numeric_shard_order", but this test can't catch a lexicographic-sort bug. The debug flavor has `split_parts=4`, and `shard_0..shard_3` sort the same either way; the bug needs 11 or more parts (`shard_10` before `shard_2`). Reversing dict order only shows the result doesn't depend on insertion order.

Either build the adapter with `split_ngram_parts >= 11` or rename the test.

Separately, this file should live in `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/`, matching the sibling `qwen3_5/` and `qwen3_8/` folders.

+    ple(x[:11], input_ids_T=ids[:11], document_positions_T=positions[:11])
+    handle.remove()
+    conv = F.conv1d(
+        F.pad(captured[-1].T[None], (9, 0)), ple.conv1d.weight, groups=1024, dilation=3
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        ple(x[:11], input_ids_T=ids[:11], document_positions_T=positions[:11]),
+        gated + F.silu(conv[0].T),
+        rtol=2e-5,
+        atol=2e-5,
+    )
+
+
+def test_qsa_selection_matches_document_local_block_oracle(config):
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    indexer = config.layers[3].attention.indexer.build()
+    indexer.init_states()
+    x = torch.randn(63, 256)
+    positions = torch.cat((torch.arange(31), torch.arange(32)))
+    padding = torch.zeros(63, dtype=torch.bool)
+    padding[5] = padding[61:] = True
+    selected, scores = indexer(
+        x, positions=positions, document_positions_T=positions, padding_mask_T=padding
+    )
+    metadata = QSAIndexMetadata.from_inputs(
+        positions, padding_mask_T=padding, compress_ratio=4
+    )
+    cached_selected, cached_scores = indexer(
+        x,
+        positions=positions,
+        document_positions_T=positions,
+        padding_mask_T=padding,
+        metadata=metadata,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(cached_selected, selected, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(cached_scores, scores, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    projection = indexer.index_qk_proj(x)
+    queries = indexer._rotate(
+        indexer.q_layernorm(projection[:, :256].unflatten(-1, (4, 64))), positions
+    )
+    pruned_queries = 0
+    for query in range(63):
+        begin = 0 if query < 31 else 31
+        visible = (
+            [token for token in range(begin, query + 1) if not padding[token]]
+            if not padding[query]
+            else []
+        )
+        complete = len(visible) // 4
+        blocks = torch.tensor(visible[: complete * 4], dtype=torch.long).reshape(
+            complete, 4
+        )
+        pooled = projection[blocks, 256:].float().mean(1)
+        keys = indexer._rotate(
+            indexer.k_layernorm(pooled).unsqueeze(1), positions[blocks[:, 0]]
+        ).squeeze(1)
+        oracle_scores = (queries[query].float() @ keys.float().T).relu().sum(0) / 8
+        winners = sorted(
+            range(complete),
+            key=lambda block: (-float(oracle_scores[block].detach()), block),
+        )[:4]
+        pruned_queries += complete > 4
+        expected = [*blocks[winners].flatten().tolist(), *visible[complete * 4 :]]
+        actual = selected[query][selected[query] >= 0].tolist()
+        assert set(actual) == set(expected)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            scores[query][scores[query].isfinite()].sort().values,
+            oracle_scores[winners].sort().values,
+            rtol=1e-5,
+            atol=1e-5,
+        )
+        assert all(token <= query for token in actual)
+    assert pruned_queries > 0
+
+
+def test_qsa_equal_score_ties_are_independent_of_future_candidates(config):
+    indexer = config.layers[3].attention.indexer.build()
+    indexer.init_states()
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        indexer.index_qk_proj.weight.zero_()
+    x = torch.randn(40, 256)
+    padding = torch.arange(40) >= 20
+    variants = (
+        (x[:20], torch.arange(20), None),
+        (x, torch.arange(40), None),
+        (x, torch.arange(20).repeat(2), None),
+        (x, torch.arange(40), padding),
+    )
+    for hidden, positions, mask in variants:
+        selected, scores = indexer(
+            hidden,
+            positions=positions,
+            document_positions_T=positions,
+            padding_mask_T=mask,
+        )
+        actual = selected[19][selected[19] >= 0].sort().values
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, torch.arange(16).int(), atol=0, rtol=0)
+        assert not scores[19].any()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("all_padding", [False, True])
+def test_qsa_output_and_backward_against_dense_selected_attention(config, all_padding):
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    indexer = config.layers[3].attention.indexer.build()
+    indexer.init_states()
+    positions = torch.arange(23)
+    padding = torch.full((23,), all_padding)
+    indices, scores = indexer(
+        torch.randn(23, 256),
+        positions=positions,
+        document_positions_T=positions,
+        padding_mask_T=padding,
+    )
+    inner = config.layers[3].attention.inner_attention.build().eval()
+    q, k, v = [
+        torch.randn(23, heads, 64, dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
+        for heads in (4, 2, 2)
+    ]
+    actual = inner(
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        selected_indices_TJ=indices,
+        scores_TB=scores,
+        scale=1 / 8,
+        enable_gqa=True,
+    )
+    mask = torch.zeros(23, 24, dtype=torch.bool).scatter(
+        1, indices.long().masked_fill(indices < 0, 23), True
+    )[:, :23]
+    expected = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+        q.permute(1, 0, 2)[None],
+        k.permute(1, 0, 2)[None],
+        v.permute(1, 0, 2)[None],
+        attn_mask=mask,
+        scale=1 / 8,
+        enable_gqa=True,
+    )[0].transpose(0, 1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-10)
+    actual_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+        actual.square().sum(), (q, k, v), retain_graph=True
+    )
+    expected_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(expected.square().sum(), (q, k, v))
+    for actual_grad, expected_grad in zip(actual_gradients, expected_gradients):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual_grad, expected_grad, rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-10)
+
+
+def test_qsa_block_kl_and_gradient_injection(config):
+    scores = torch.tensor(
+        [[0.0, math.log(2), math.log(4)], [-torch.inf] * 3], requires_grad=True
+    )
+    teacher = torch.tensor([[0.25, 0.5, 0.25], [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]], requires_grad=True)
+    actual = QSAIndexerLoss.block_kl(scores, teacher)
+    expected = sum(
+        p * math.log(p / q) for p, q in zip((0.25, 0.5, 0.25), (1 / 7, 2 / 7, 4 / 7))
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, torch.tensor(expected))
+    actual.backward()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        scores.grad[0], torch.tensor([1 / 7 - 0.25, 2 / 7 - 0.5, 4 / 7 - 0.25])
+    )
+    assert not scores.grad[1].any() and teacher.grad is None
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    attention = config.layers[3].attention.build()
+    attention.init_states()
+    x = torch.randn(31, 256, requires_grad=True)
+    positions = torch.arange(31)
+    output = attention(
+        x,
+        None,
+        positions,
+        document_positions_T=positions,
+        aux_loss_denominator=torch.tensor(31.0),
+    )
+    output.square().mean().backward()
+    assert attention.indexer.index_qk_proj.weight.grad.norm() > 0
+    assert torch.isfinite(x.grad).all()
+    assert attention.inner_attention.indexer_loss.instance_acc > 0
+    attention.inner_attention.indexer_loss._reset_accumulators()
+    assert attention.inner_attention.indexer_loss.instance_acc == 0
+
+
+def test_qsa_auxiliary_gradient_only_updates_the_indexer(config):
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    attention = config.layers[3].attention.build().train()
+    attention.init_states()
+    x = torch.randn(31, 256, requires_grad=True)
+    positions = torch.arange(31)
+    output = attention(
+        x,
+        None,
+        positions,
+        document_positions_T=positions,
+        aux_loss_denominator=torch.tensor(31.0),
+    )
+    # A zero LM carrier isolates the injected auxiliary objective.
+    (output.sum() * 0).backward()
+    assert x.grad is not None and not x.grad.any()
+    assert attention.indexer.index_qk_proj.weight.grad.norm() > 0
+    for module in (attention.wq, attention.wk, attention.wv, attention.wo):
+        assert module.weight.grad is None or not module.weight.grad.any()
+
+
+def test_deltanet_uses_sigmoid_output_gate(config):
+    norm = config.layers[0].attention.norm.build()
+    norm.init_states()
+    x = torch.randn(5, 4, 128)
+    gate = torch.randn_like(x)
+    expected = F.rms_norm(x.float(), (128,), eps=1e-6) * gate.sigmoid()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(norm(x, gate), expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("compiled", [False, True])
+def test_router_bfloat16_ties_mixing_and_backward(config, compiled):
+    """Round before expert selection and retain differentiable normalized gates."""
+    router = config.layers[3].feed_forward.router.build().bfloat16().eval()
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        router.gate.weight.zero_()
+        router.gate.weight[0, :2] = torch.tensor([1.0, 1 / 256])
+        router.gate.weight[1, 0] = 1
+        router.gate.weight[2, :2] = torch.tensor([1.0, 1 / 256])
+    router.gate.inplace_wgrad_accum = False
+    tested_router = torch.compile(router, fullgraph=True) if compiled else router
+    x = torch.ones(3, 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+    reference_weight = router.gate.weight.detach().float().requires_grad_()
+    reference_x = x.detach().float().requires_grad_()
+    logits = F.linear(reference_x, reference_weight).to(x.dtype).float()
+    reference_scores, reference_ids = logits.softmax(-1).topk(2, -1)
+    reference_scores = (reference_scores / reference_scores.sum(-1, keepdim=True)).to(
+        x.dtype
+    )
+    scores, indices, routing = tested_router(x)
+    expected_routing = torch.zeros_like(logits, dtype=torch.bool).scatter(
+        -1, reference_ids, True
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(routing, expected_routing)
+    assert not torch.equal(
+        indices.sort(-1).values,
+        F.linear(reference_x, reference_weight).topk(2, -1).indices.sort(-1).values,
+    )
+    actual_weights = torch.zeros_like(logits).scatter(-1, indices, scores.float())
+    expected_weights = torch.zeros_like(logits).scatter(
+        -1, reference_ids, reference_scores.float()
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_weights, expected_weights, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    objective = torch.arange(8, dtype=torch.float32)
+    actual_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+        (actual_weights * objective).sum(), (x, router.gate.weight)
+    )
+    expected_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+        (expected_weights * objective).sum(), (reference_x, reference_weight)
+    )
+    for actual_grad, expected_grad in zip(actual_gradients, expected_gradients):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            actual_grad.float(), expected_grad.to(x.dtype).float(), atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-2
+        )
+
+
+def test_adapter_roundtrip_and_numeric_shard_order(config):
+    model = config.build()
+    model.init_states()
+    adapter = Qwen38FlashNextStateDictAdapter(config, None)
+    state = model.state_dict()
+    hf = adapter.to_hf(state)

The script depends on private test internals and monkeypatches:
- It imports `_reference_causal_conv1d_varlen` from a GPU test module (here and again at L769).
- It patches `gdn._causal_conv1d_varlen` and replaces the kernel object.
- It patches `RoutedExperts.forward` with an FP32 oracle (L220-222).

Any rename in those tests silently breaks this script, and the parity check no longer runs the production path. `_run` is also a single ~1000-line function, where sibling scripts (qwen3_5: 447 lines) split into build/run/compare.

Please either promote the reference kernels to a non-test, non-private location that both consumers import, or drop the patched variants. The script is 1,184 lines; the patched variants are a large share of it.

## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Rebase and review status

Current head: `a92514131a2944b744a1bf512972f9a972fed83b`. The stack is rebased onto fetched upstream main
`73c4ebdac57de0d89bb20d5dfabed340449c8b0d`; commit prefixes now match the four PR titles.
The latest `pr-review` skill and checklist were read from this rebased checkout.

The rebase updates the `PrecisionConfig` parallelize contract, checks QSA
accelerator capture before dynamic metadata construction, preserves Flash-Next's
BF16 GDN parameter policy, restores the PP test imports, and retains upstream's
redundant-test deletions. Current exact-prefix checks: all-file pre-commit passes
and 50 CPU tests pass. The full-stack CPU run hides GPUs so the
upstream CPU FSDP test does not select the unavailable FA4 package.

[Claude's review of #5782](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782#pullrequestreview-5761648327)
still has open FSDP/indexer and QSA training-memory findings. Earlier local
approval claims are withdrawn. HF/GPU/convergence results below are historical
captures at their stated SHAs; this rebase has not received fresh GPU validation.
The human summary placeholder is retained for the author to complete before review.

Planned next revision:

1. Connect a finite zero indexer gradient on empty/short-document ranks and define frozen-indexer behavior when no KL objective is configured.
2. Reuse compatible Attention Gym selection, qualify public efficient SDPA and per-query-chunk remat, and measure saved forward/backward memory. Existing [#678](https://github.com/meta-pytorch/attention-gym/pull/678)/[#679](https://github.com/meta-pytorch/attention-gym/pull/679) lack the complete grouped separate-K/V backward path.
3. Simplify the norm/head-count plumbing, adapter handling, checkpoint fixture and parity harness; retain behavioral tests and clarify table-memory/reset semantics.
4. Validate the resulting stack on the requested DCT GB300 tenant before asking for re-review.

## Why

TorchTitan cannot build or train the released Flash-Next architecture. Qwen3.5
already supplies its GDN, gated shared experts, multimodal preprocessing,
vision encoder, FSDP and optimizer hooks, but the decoder has different residual,
lexical and sparse-attention computation. This PR adds those differences using
the existing model lifecycle and component configs.

Component reuse needs public Qwen3.5 config factories, ordinary `Linear.Config`
router gates, and a shared structural annotation contract for QSA metadata.
This model supplies the concrete consumer of all three shared API changes.

For a packed document with T tokens and hidden width D, a decoder block carries
four streams instead of one:

```text
[T, 4*D] -> PLE lookup/injection -> gated read [T, D]
          -> GDN or selected QSA -> gated residual write [T, 4*D]
          -> gated read [T, D] -> shared routed MoE -> gated write [T, 4*D]
```

Original token IDs and document positions reach PLE independently of multimodal
rotary coordinates. Masked/padded tokens do not contribute to MoE auxiliary
counts. The optional indexer-teacher objective trains only the indexer.

## What changed

- Expose `make_qwen35_deltanet_config` and `make_qwen35_vision_encoder_config`,
  accept the shared `Linear.Config` router-gate base, and use structural
  attention metadata annotation. Factory-callsite renames are mechanical;
  shared arithmetic and parameter layouts are unchanged.
- Add model-specific gated residual, offset/gated normalization, partial MRoPE,
  n-gram PLE, rounded router scoring and chunked selected-token QSA reference code.
- Reuse Qwen3.5's GDN/vision config factories and training/FSDP lifecycle.
- Export the standard model/flavor/build API and explicit indexer-loss config.
- Add strict HF mappings for all 1,627 released decoder/vision keys, including
  numeric lexical shard ordering; the 31 MTP keys are outside this model.
- Add independent feature/backward tests and the same-weight HF parity harness.

This initial increment supports FSDP. TP/SP and EP follow in `2/n`, the shared
deterministic GDN policy in `3/n`, and PP in `4/n`. CP remains unsupported.

## User-facing changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Qwen config factories are private and shared gate typing excludes ordinary `Linear` | Public factories, the shared `Linear.Config` base and structural metadata annotation support the new model |
| Flash-Next has no model/flavor factory | `build_model_config("debugmodel", seq_len=64, parallelism=ParallelismConfig())` builds the reduced decoder; the released flavor is available for meta construction |
| Flash-Next checkpoint has no TorchTitan adapter | The native/HF adapter maps the released decoder and vision tensors and excludes unsupported MTP |
| Flash-Next image/video tokens have no training path | The inherited Qwen3.5 processor and vision encoder fuse features into the model's placeholder positions |

## Numerics

The shared API refactor changes no arithmetic or tensor layouts. Its preserved
Qwen3.5 MoE video comparison uses actual base `01586df70d7599d59a87663f39670a8c694924c3`
and head `06cd1fb1c4e1b340f5398c5b4ed1459530589d64`: ten steps on one GB300,
seed 42 and strict deterministic execution. All 20 full-precision loss/grad_norm
values agree bitwise; loss goes from 13.087042808532715 to 0.34375783801078796.
This historical comparison covers the original shared API refactor; later upstream dtype changes were outside that capture.

Pinned checkpoint `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` revision
`de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540`; Transformers revision
`494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab`.

The reduced eight-layer model retains both GDN/QSA, all four streams, PLE,
and routed/shared experts. Its 39-token text fixture exercises real pruning.
CPU FP32 and BF16 train/eval comparisons pass: full logits, normalized CE,
embedding-input gradients and all 184 mapped decoder parameter gradients.
Full image/video fusion, MRoPE and masked CE additionally compare both pixel
input gradients and all 225 decoder/vision parameter gradients. Standalone
vision compares all 41 parameter gradients.

On the previously reviewed prefix `b9bdfa4da3ca1708359834cad53027abca181272`, the CPU
FP32/BF16 and CUDA BF16 harnesses all pass. The CUDA multimodal comparison has
CE 4.157130241394043 versus HF 4.157289981842041 and maximum logit difference
0.00390625. Both pixel inputs have nonzero gradients, and all 225 mapped
parameter gradients pass their original RMS/infinity bounds.

BF16 multimodal routing uses ordinary seeded projections because near-tied
expert cutoffs amplified the shared fused GDN's BF16 rounding. The recorded
seeds are 30003/31002/32004/33011/34001/35007/36023/37036. All 128 query/layer
cutoffs match naturally and exceed a preregistered margin: four times both
actual raw-logit drift and dtype epsilon times logit scale, with a 0.002 floor.
The minimum observed margin ratio is 1.0463576. Primary text, standalone vision
and FP32 multimodal weights are unchanged; no routes or scores are imposed.

Real FSDP2 uses the same FP32 checkpoint and global 512-token batch as the
baseline. All 190 preclip reconstructed parameter gradients pass the original
bounds; maximum absolute difference is 3.725290298461914e-09. This was captured
at `a1e1d506c`; subsequent port amendments changed the reference fixture and
README, then migrated two recipe settings to upstream's configurable
TensorBoard logger API. The model computation and sharding are unchanged.
No fitted gradient scaling is applied.

The reference results above identify their actual capture revisions. The current
base and exact-head CPU/lint results are recorded separately above. New GPU
qualification is part of the revision plan.

| Training check | GPUs / steps | Full-precision result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C4, reduced eight-layer decoder, sequence 256, official tokenizer/vocabulary | 1 GB300 / 100 | Loss 12.553109169006348 -> 7.390992164611816; first/last ten means 12.4797701836 -> 7.9403163433 |
| Actual image/video debug training recipe | 1 GB300 / 10 | Loss 7.678964614868164 -> 3.388758420944214 |

Both training checks use seed 42 and strict deterministic execution. C4 retains
the reduced PLE table and uses vocabulary 248320 and EOS 248044 with streamed
`allenai/c4`, English training split. Its loss and gradient norm at all 100
steps are also bitwise identical before/after the padding-mask callsite cleanup.

## Testing

Current rebased prefix: `a92514131a2944b744a1bf512972f9a972fed83b`. Its all-file pre-commit hooks and
50 CPU config/feature cases pass. Numerical captures below retain
their original source references.

- Exact-prefix `pre-commit run --all-files`: all hooks pass.
- Exact-prefix CPU feature/config tests: 50 pass.
- Audited every shared factory caller, router config subclass and metadata
  runtime check; the same 50-case prefix includes the shared build/config tests.
- FP32/BF16 CPU HF harness with 39 tokens and full multimodal backward: pass.
- CUDA BF16 HF harness with 39 tokens and full multimodal backward: pass.
- Real FSDP2 checkpoint/batch/preclip-gradient comparison: pass.
- C4 convergence (100 steps) and image/video training (10 steps): pass.
- Claude's FSDP/indexer and QSA saved-memory must-fix findings remain open; the earlier local approval claim is withdrawn.

```bash
pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_qwen3_8_flash_next.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_build_model_config.py -q
python -m scripts.checkpoint_conversion.numerical_tests_qwen3_8_flash_next \
  --device cuda --backbone-dtype bfloat16 --full-token-count 39
NGPU=1 MODULE=torchtitan_recipes.tests.models.qwen3_8_flash_next \
  CONFIG=qwen38_flash_next_debugmodel_mm ./run_train.sh
```

## Alternatives considered

- Reimplement shared GDN/vision or add model-specific flags to common modules:
  rejected because the public Qwen3.5 config factories already supply both.
- Full dense attention with a sparse mask: the selected-token implementation
  expresses the released block/tail semantics directly, but its saved training
  memory is unresolved and requires the revision described above.

Full released-checkpoint materialization, 51.2B-table distributed conversion,
full-size training, inference KV caching and MTP are outside the validated scope.
The SDPA MATH path retains activations across query chunks; full-scale memory
and throughput are unqualified.

## Stack

This stack supersedes [the earlier all-in-one draft #5655](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5655).
Its original branch and worktree are retained for reference.

Draft 1/n of the Flash-Next implementation.

- [1/n Add Flash-Next model, FSDP and checkpoint reference coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782)
- [2/n Add tensor and expert parallelism with batched QSA teachers](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5783)
- [3/n Honor deterministic GDN normalization](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5784)
- [4/n Add pipeline stages, remat and numerical integration coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5785)

This combined model increment includes the shared API changes from #5781
and targets `main`. Merge the stack in order.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3

+"""Same-weight component, block, vision and full-logit Flash-Next parity.
+
+Install transformers at 494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab, then run:
+python -m scripts.checkpoint_conversion.numerical_tests_qwen3_8_flash_next
+The reduced fixture retains every backbone feature. Components and gradients
+use FP32; the recurrent backbone uses BF16, as required by its shared kernel.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import copy
+import json
+from contextlib import ExitStack
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+from torch.nn.attention import sdpa_kernel, SDPBackend
+
+from torchtitan.config.parallelism import ParallelismConfig
+from torchtitan.models.common.attention import InnerAttention
+from torchtitan.models.qwen3_8_flash_next import build_model_config
+from torchtitan.models.qwen3_8_flash_next.state_dict_adapter import (
+    Qwen38FlashNextStateDictAdapter,
+)
+
+REFERENCE_REVISION = "494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab"
+CHECKPOINT_REVISION = "de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540"
+
+# T = packed tokens, D = model dimension, C = residual streams * D,
+# E = experts, K = selected experts, V = vocabulary.
+BF16_EPS = torch.finfo(torch.bfloat16).eps
+FIXTURE_SEED = 44
+VISION_SEED = 1729
+INDEXER_SEEDS = {3: 10001, 7: 20008}
+# Qualified against both CPU GDN normalization baselines; CUDA is qualified
+# independently. These are ordinary Normal(0, 0.02) CPU-generated projections.
+MM_ROUTER_SEEDS = {
+    0: 30003,
+    1: 31002,
+    2: 32004,
+    3: 33011,
+    4: 34001,
+    5: 35007,
+    6: 36023,
+    7: 37036,
+}
+
+
+class ReferenceVisionAttention(InnerAttention):
+    """Differentiable CPU oracle for the vision encoder's packed mask."""
+
+    def forward(self, q_THK, k_THK, v_THV, *, attention_metadata, **kwargs):
+        indices_T = torch.arange(q_THK.shape[0], device=q_THK.device)
+        mask_TT = attention_metadata.mask_mod(
+            0, 0, indices_T[:, None], indices_T[None, :]
+        )
+        with sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.MATH):
+            output_1HTV = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+                q_THK.transpose(0, 1)[None],
+                k_THK.transpose(0, 1)[None],
+                v_THV.transpose(0, 1)[None],
+                attn_mask=mask_TT,
+                scale=kwargs.get("scale"),
+                enable_gqa=kwargs.get("enable_gqa", False),
+            )
+        return output_1HTV[0].transpose(0, 1)
+
+
+def reference_text_config() -> Any:
+    from transformers.models.qwen4_exp.configuration_qwen4_exp import Qwen4ExpTextConfig
+
+    return Qwen4ExpTextConfig(
+        hidden_size=256,
+        vocab_size=64,
+        num_hidden_layers=8,
+        num_attention_heads=4,
+        num_key_value_heads=2,
+        head_dim=64,
+        max_position_embeddings=64,
+        linear_num_key_heads=2,
+        linear_num_value_heads=4,
+        linear_key_head_dim=128,
+        linear_value_head_dim=128,
+        num_experts=8,
+        num_experts_per_tok=2,
+        moe_intermediate_size=128,
+        shared_expert_intermediate_size=128,
+        hc_count=4,
+        hc_lowrank=32,
+        ple_layer_ids=[2],
+        ple_embed_dim=256,
+        heads_per_ngram=2,
+        ngram_vocab_size_base=257,
+        split_ngram_parts=4,
+        eos_token_id=63,
+        indexer_n_heads=4,
+        indexer_kv_heads=1,
+        indexer_head_dim=64,
+        indexer_budget=16,
+        indexer_compress_ratio=4,
+        output_gate_type="sigmoid",
+        rope_parameters={
+            "rope_type": "default",
+            "rope_theta": 10_000_000,
+            "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25,
+            "mrope_section": [3, 3, 2],
+            "mrope_interleaved": True,
+        },
+        use_cache=False,
+    )
+
+
+def run(*, device: str, backbone_dtype: str, full_token_count: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    with ExitStack() as reference_stack:
+        reference_stack.enter_context(sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.MATH))
+        return _run(
+            device=device,
+            backbone_dtype=backbone_dtype,
+            full_token_count=full_token_count,
+            reference_stack=reference_stack,
+        )
+
+
+def _run(
+    *,
+    device: str,
+    backbone_dtype: str,
+    full_token_count: int,
+    reference_stack: ExitStack,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    from transformers.models.qwen4_exp.configuration_qwen4_exp import (
+        Qwen4ExpConfig,
+        Qwen4ExpVisionConfig,
+    )
+    from transformers.models.qwen4_exp.modeling_qwen4_exp import (
+        Qwen4ExpForCausalLM,
+        Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration,
+        Qwen4ExpVisionModel,
+    )
+
+    selected_dtype = getattr(torch, backbone_dtype)
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
+    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("highest")
+    torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False
+    config = build_model_config(
+        "debugmodel_mm", seq_len=64, parallelism=ParallelismConfig()
+    )
+    for layer in config.layers:
+        layer.feed_forward.router.aux_loss = None
+    vision_config = config.vision_encoder
+    assert vision_config is not None
+    config.vision_encoder = None
+    config.vocab_size = (
+        config.tok_embeddings.num_embeddings
+    ) = config.lm_head.out_features = 64
+    config.layers[1].ple.ple_embedding.vocab_size = 64
+    config.layers[1].ple.ple_embedding.eos_token_id = 63
+    hf_config = reference_text_config()
+    hf_config._attn_implementation = "sdpa"
+    hf = Qwen4ExpForCausalLM(hf_config).to(device).eval()
+    native = config.build().to(device).eval()
+    adapter = Qwen38FlashNextStateDictAdapter(config, None)
+    native.init_states()
+    native.load_state_dict(adapter.from_hf(hf.state_dict()), strict=True)
+    if torch.device(device).type == "cpu":
+        cpu_threads = torch.get_num_threads()
+        torch.set_num_threads(1)
+        reference_stack.callback(torch.set_num_threads, cpu_threads)
+        # The AArch64 nightly's oneDNN Conv3d input backward fails a direct
+        # Linear-equivalence check. Native CPU convolution preserves that
+        # equivalence and keeps the reference's image gradients meaningful.
+        reference_stack.enter_context(torch.backends.mkldnn.flags(enabled=False))
+        from tests.unit_tests.gpu.models.qwen3_5.test_qwen3_5_deltanet import (
+            _reference_causal_conv1d_varlen,
+            ReferenceGatedDeltaKernel,
+        )
+        from torchtitan.models.common.attention.gdn import GDN
+
+        for layer in native.layers.values():
+            if isinstance(layer.attention, GDN):
+                layer.attention.inner_attention.kernel = ReferenceGatedDeltaKernel()
+        reference_stack.enter_context(
+            patch(
+                "torchtitan.models.common.attention.gdn._causal_conv1d_varlen",
+                _reference_causal_conv1d_varlen,
+            )
+        )
+    if selected_dtype == torch.float32:
+        from torchtitan.models.common.moe.moe import RoutedExperts
+
+        def fp32_experts(
+            self, x_TD, topk_scores_TK, topk_expert_ids_TK, routing_map_TE, **kwargs
+        ):
+            # The shared routed path uses BF16 operands. This independent FP32
+            # equation oracle checks architecture gradients without quantizing.
+            output_TD = torch.zeros_like(x_TD)
+            for expert_id in range(self.w13.weight.shape[0]):
+                tokens_R, slots_R = torch.where(topk_expert_ids_TK == expert_id)
+                gate_up_R2F = torch.nn.functional.linear(
+                    x_TD[tokens_R], self.w13.weight[expert_id].flatten(0, 1)
+                ).unflatten(-1, self.w13.weight.shape[1:3])
+                hidden_RF = self.activation_fn(gate_up_R2F)
+                expert_RD = torch.nn.functional.linear(
+                    hidden_RF, self.w2.weight[expert_id]
+                )
+                output_TD = output_TD.index_add(
+                    0, tokens_R, expert_RD * topk_scores_TK[tokens_R, slots_R, None]
+                )
+            return output_TD
+
+        reference_stack.enter_context(
+            patch.object(RoutedExperts, "forward", fp32_experts)
+        )
+    fixture_generator = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(FIXTURE_SEED)
+
+    def fixture_randn(shape, *, requires_grad=False):
+        return (
+            torch.randn(shape, generator=fixture_generator, device="cpu")
+            .to(device)
+            .requires_grad_(requires_grad)
+        )
+
+    positions = torch.arange(39, device=device)
+    tokens = torch.randint(0, 63, (39,), generator=fixture_generator, device="cpu").to(
+        device
+    )
+    tokens[7] = 63
+    hidden = fixture_randn((39, 1024), requires_grad=True)
+    results: dict[str, Any] = {}
+
+    def compare(
+        name: str,
+        actual: torch.Tensor,
+        expected: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        atol: float = 2e-5,
+        rtol: float = 2e-5,
+    ) -> None:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            actual,
+            expected,
+            atol=atol,
+            rtol=rtol,
+            msg=lambda message: f"{name}: {message}",
+        )
+        difference = actual.detach().double() - expected.detach().double()
+        results[name] = {
+            "max_abs": float(difference.abs().max()),
+            "rms": float(difference.square().mean().sqrt()),
+            "relative_l2": float(difference.norm() / expected.detach().double().norm()),
+            "atol": atol,
+            "rtol": rtol,
+        }
+
+    def compare_gradients(
+        name: str,
+        actual_loss: torch.Tensor,
+        expected_loss: torch.Tensor,
+        input_TC: torch.Tensor,
+        actual_module: torch.nn.Module,
+        expected_module: torch.nn.Module,
+    ) -> None:
+        actual_parameters = dict(actual_module.named_parameters())
+        expected_parameters = dict(expected_module.named_parameters())
+        assert actual_parameters.keys() == expected_parameters.keys()
+        actual_grads = torch.autograd.grad(
+            actual_loss, (input_TC, *actual_parameters.values())
+        )
+        expected_grads = torch.autograd.grad(
+            expected_loss, (input_TC, *expected_parameters.values())
+        )
+        for field, actual_grad, expected_grad in zip(
+            ("input", *actual_parameters), actual_grads, expected_grads
+        ):
+            compare(
+                f"{name}_gradient/{field}",
+                actual_grad,
+                expected_grad,
+                atol=3e-6,
+                rtol=3e-5,
+            )
+
+    def compare_gradient(name, actual, expected, *, atol, rtol, compute_dtype=None):
+        if (
+            compute_dtype != torch.bfloat16
+            and actual.dtype != torch.bfloat16
+            and expected.dtype != torch.bfloat16
+        ):
+            compare(name, actual, expected, atol=atol, rtol=rtol)
+            return
+        # Packed native projections and separate HF projections round BF16
+        # input-gradient sums differently. Bound both RMS and peak error; an
+        # elementwise relative check is ill-conditioned near cancellation.
+        reference = expected.detach().double()
+        difference = actual.detach().double() - reference
+        error_rms = difference.square().mean().sqrt()
+        reference_rms = reference.square().mean().sqrt()
+        assert error_rms <= atol + rtol * reference_rms, name
+        assert difference.abs().max() <= atol + rtol * reference.abs().max(), name
+        results[name] = {
+            "max_abs": float(difference.abs().max()),
+            "rms": float(error_rms),
+            "relative_l2": float(difference.norm() / reference.norm()),
+            "atol": atol,
+            "rtol": rtol,
+            "comparison": "RMS and infinity norm",
+        }
+
+    def compare_mapped_parameter_gradients(
+        name,
+        actual_module,
+        expected_module,
+        mapping,
+        *,
+        actual_prefix="",
+        expected_prefix="",
+        required_lm_head_gradient=None,
+        compute_dtype=None,
+        atol=3e-6,
+        rtol=3e-5,
+    ):
+        expected_source = {
+            expected_prefix + key: value.grad
+            for key, value in expected_module.named_parameters()
+            if value.grad is not None
+        }
+        if required_lm_head_gradient is not None:
+            # The reused full-model adapter requires an LM-head entry, even
+            # when checking vision alone. Its gradient was already checked.
+            expected_source["lm_head.weight"] = required_lm_head_gradient
+        expected_gradients = mapping.from_hf(expected_source)
+        if required_lm_head_gradient is not None:
+            expected_gradients.pop("lm_head.weight")
+        actual_norm_squared = 0.0
+        expected_norm_squared = 0.0
+        gradient_dot = 0.0
+        count = 0
+        for key, parameter in actual_module.named_parameters():
+            actual_grad = parameter.grad
+            expected_grad = expected_gradients.pop(actual_prefix + key, None)
+            assert (actual_grad is None) == (
+                expected_grad is None
+            ), f"{name}/{key}: gradient presence differs"
+            if actual_grad is None:
+                continue
+            compare_gradient(
+                f"{name}/{key}",
+                actual_grad,
+                expected_grad,
+                atol=atol,
+                rtol=rtol,
+                compute_dtype=compute_dtype,
+            )
+            actual_norm = actual_grad.double().norm()
+            expected_norm = expected_grad.double().norm()
+            entry = results[f"{name}/{key}"]
+            entry["norm_ratio"] = (
+                float(actual_norm / expected_norm) if expected_norm else None
+            )
+            entry["cosine"] = (
+                float(
+                    torch.dot(
+                        actual_grad.double().flatten(), expected_grad.double().flatten()
+                    )
+                    / (actual_norm * expected_norm)
+                )
+                if actual_norm and expected_norm
+                else None
+            )
+            actual_norm_squared += float(actual_norm.square())
+            expected_norm_squared += float(expected_norm.square())
+            gradient_dot += float(
+                torch.dot(
+                    actual_grad.double().flatten(), expected_grad.double().flatten()
+                )
+            )
+            count += 1
+        assert (
+            not expected_gradients
+        ), f"{name}: unmapped gradients: {list(expected_gradients)}"
+        actual_global_norm = actual_norm_squared**0.5
+        reference_global_norm = expected_norm_squared**0.5
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            actual_global_norm, reference_global_norm, atol=atol, rtol=rtol
+        )
+        global_cosine = gradient_dot / (actual_global_norm * reference_global_norm)
+        assert global_cosine >= 1 - rtol**2, name
+        results[name + "/global"] = {
+            "parameter_tensors": count,
+            "actual_grad_norm": actual_norm_squared**0.5,
+            "reference_grad_norm": expected_norm_squared**0.5,
+            "norm_ratio": (actual_norm_squared / expected_norm_squared) ** 0.5,
+            "cosine": global_cosine,
+        }
+
+    # Norms and mixing gradients are checked before the recurrent stack.
+    actual, _, write = native.layers["0"].attn_hyper_connection(hidden)
+    expected, _, hf_write = hf.model.layers[0].attn_hyper_connection(hidden[None])
+    compare("residual_read", actual, expected[0])
+    compare("residual_write", write, hf_write[0])
+    compare_gradients(
+        "residual",
+        actual.square().mean() + write.square().mean(),
+        expected.square().mean() + hf_write.square().mean(),
+        hidden,
+        native.layers["0"].attn_hyper_connection,
+        hf.model.layers[0].attn_hyper_connection,
+    )
+    ple = native.layers["1"].ple
+    hf_ple = hf.model.layers[1].ple
+    # Exercise convolution backwards with nonzero weights; released initialization is zero.
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        hf_ple.conv1d.weight.copy_(
+            torch.empty(hf_ple.conv1d.weight.shape, device="cpu")
+            .uniform_(-0.02, 0.02, generator=fixture_generator)
+            .to(hf_ple.conv1d.weight)
+        )
+        ple.conv1d.weight.copy_(hf_ple.conv1d.weight)
+    hidden = hidden.detach().requires_grad_()
+    actual = ple(hidden, input_ids_T=tokens, document_positions_T=positions)
+    expected = hf_ple(hidden[None], tokens[None], None)[0]
+    compare("ple", actual, expected)
+    compare_gradients(
+        "ple", actual.square().mean(), expected.square().mean(), hidden, ple, hf_ple
+    )
+    x = fixture_randn((39, 256))

+            if hashed >= 1 << 63:

+def test_qsa_block_kl_and_gradient_injection(config):
+    scores = torch.tensor(
+        [[0.0, math.log(2), math.log(4)], [-torch.inf] * 3], requires_grad=True
+    )
+    teacher = torch.tensor([[0.25, 0.5, 0.25], [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]], requires_grad=True)
+    actual = QSAIndexerLoss.block_kl(scores, teacher)
+    expected = sum(
+        p * math.log(p / q) for p, q in zip((0.25, 0.5, 0.25), (1 / 7, 2 / 7, 4 / 7))
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, torch.tensor(expected))
+    actual.backward()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        scores.grad[0], torch.tensor([1 / 7 - 0.25, 2 / 7 - 0.5, 4 / 7 - 0.25])
+    )
+    assert not scores.grad[1].any() and teacher.grad is None
+    torch.manual_seed(42)

+def test_router_bfloat16_ties_mixing_and_backward(config, compiled):
+    """Round before expert selection and retain differentiable normalized gates."""
+    router = config.layers[3].feed_forward.router.build().bfloat16().eval()
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        router.gate.weight.zero_()
+        router.gate.weight[0, :2] = torch.tensor([1.0, 1 / 256])
+        router.gate.weight[1, 0] = 1
+        router.gate.weight[2, :2] = torch.tensor([1.0, 1 / 256])
+    router.gate.inplace_wgrad_accum = False
+    tested_router = torch.compile(router, fullgraph=True) if compiled else router
+    x = torch.ones(3, 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+    reference_weight = router.gate.weight.detach().float().requires_grad_()
+    reference_x = x.detach().float().requires_grad_()
+    logits = F.linear(reference_x, reference_weight).to(x.dtype).float()
+    reference_scores, reference_ids = logits.softmax(-1).topk(2, -1)
+    reference_scores = (reference_scores / reference_scores.sum(-1, keepdim=True)).to(
+        x.dtype
+    )
+    scores, indices, routing = tested_router(x)
+    expected_routing = torch.zeros_like(logits, dtype=torch.bool).scatter(
+        -1, reference_ids, True
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(routing, expected_routing)
+    assert not torch.equal(
+        indices.sort(-1).values,
+        F.linear(reference_x, reference_weight).topk(2, -1).indices.sort(-1).values,
+    )
+    actual_weights = torch.zeros_like(logits).scatter(-1, indices, scores.float())
+    expected_weights = torch.zeros_like(logits).scatter(
+        -1, reference_ids, reference_scores.float()
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_weights, expected_weights, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    objective = torch.arange(8, dtype=torch.float32)
+    actual_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+        (actual_weights * objective).sum(), (x, router.gate.weight)
+    )
+    expected_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+        (expected_weights * objective).sum(), (reference_x, reference_weight)
+    )
+    for actual_grad, expected_grad in zip(actual_gradients, expected_gradients):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            actual_grad.float(), expected_grad.to(x.dtype).float(), atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-2
+        )
+

+def test_packed_padding_is_excluded_from_moe_auxiliary_gradients(config, all_padding):
+    from torchtitan.models.common.aux_loss import AuxLoss
+    from torchtitan.models.common.moe.moe import MicrobatchWiseLoadBalanceLoss
+
+    config.layers = [copy.deepcopy(config.layers[3])]
+    config.layers[0].attention.inner_attention.indexer_loss = None
+    config.layers[
+        0
+    ].feed_forward.router.aux_loss = MicrobatchWiseLoadBalanceLoss.Config(
+        coeff=1.0, reduce_mesh="loss"
+    )
+    saved_counts, saved_acc = AuxLoss._group_counts.copy(), AuxLoss.group_acc.copy()
+    handles = []
+    try:
+        torch.manual_seed(42)
+        model = config.build().train()
+        model.init_states()
+        router = model.layers["0"].feed_forward.router
+        captured = []
+        handles = [
+            router.register_forward_pre_hook(
+                lambda module, inputs: captured.append(inputs[0])
+            ),
+            router.register_forward_hook(
+                lambda module, inputs, output: captured.append(output[0])
+            ),
+        ]
+        ids = torch.randint(0, 63, (12,))
+        positions = torch.cat((torch.arange(5), torch.arange(7)))
+        padding = torch.ones(12, dtype=torch.bool)
+        if not all_padding:
+            padding[:4] = padding[5:9] = False
+        denominator = (~padding).sum().float().clamp_min(1)
+        metadata = model._get_attention_metadata(
+            positions=positions, padding_mask=padding
+        )
+        model(
+            ids,
+            positions=positions,
+            document_positions=positions,
+            ple_input_ids=ids,
+            attention_metadata=metadata,
+            padding_mask=padding,
+            aux_loss_denominators=denominator[None],
+        )
+        # Independent leaves isolate the auxiliary gradient from the LM loss.
+        x_TD = captured[0].detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
+        weight_ED = router.gate.weight.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
+        probabilities_TE = F.softmax(
+            F.linear(x_TD, weight_ED), dim=-1, dtype=torch.float32
+        )
+        ids_TK = probabilities_TE.topk(router.top_k, dim=-1).indices
+        valid_T = ~padding
+        num_experts = probabilities_TE.shape[-1]
+        counts_E = (F.one_hot(ids_TK, num_experts).sum(1) * valid_T[:, None]).sum(0)
+        frequency_E = num_experts * counts_E.float() / counts_E.sum().clamp_min(1)
+        score_sums_E = (
+            probabilities_TE / probabilities_TE.sum(-1, keepdim=True) * valid_T[:, None]
+        ).sum(0)
+        expected_loss = (frequency_E * score_sums_E).sum() / denominator
+        expected_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(expected_loss, (x_TD, weight_ED))
+        actual_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+            captured[1].sum() * 0, (captured[0], router.gate.weight)
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            router.tokens_per_expert_E,
+            counts_E.to(router.tokens_per_expert_E),
+            atol=0,
+            rtol=0,
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            router.aux_loss.instance_acc, expected_loss.detach(), atol=1e-7, rtol=1e-5
+        )
+        for actual, expected in zip(actual_gradients, expected_gradients):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=1e-7, rtol=1e-5)
+        assert torch.count_nonzero(actual_gradients[0][padding]) == 0
+    finally:
+        for handle in handles:
+            handle.remove()
+        AuxLoss._group_counts.clear()
+        AuxLoss._group_counts.update(saved_counts)
+        AuxLoss.group_acc.clear()
+        AuxLoss.group_acc.update(saved_acc)
+

+# Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
+
+Flash-Next reuses Qwen3.5's Gated DeltaNet, vision encoder, FSDP and optimizer
+lifecycle. Its model package implements four-stream gated residuals, sparse
+QSA attention, lexical embeddings, and the checkpoint's router rounding.
+
+## Reference and checkpoint
+
+- [Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next),
+  checkpoint revision `de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540`.
+- Transformers `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM`, `Qwen4ExpVisionModel`, and
+  `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` at revision
+  `494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab`.
+- The adapter inventories 1,627 released decoder/vision keys on meta tensors.
+  It packs the 128 numeric lexical shards in checkpoint order. The 31 MTP keys
+  are outside this training model and are skipped with a warning.
+
+## Architecture
+
+| Path | Released shape or configuration |
+| --- | --- |
+| Decoder | 48 layers, model width 2,560, vocabulary 248,320 |
+| Gated residual | Four streams, grouped offset RMSNorm, gate rank 320 |
+| Attention | Three shared GDN layers followed by one QSA layer |
+| QSA | 24 query / 2 KV heads, head width 256, partial MRoPE |
+| Indexer | Four heads of width 128, four-token blocks, 2,048-token budget plus causal tail |
+| MoE | 512 experts, top 10, routed/shared width 640, sigmoid shared gate |
+| PLE | Layer 2, 16 bigram/trigram heads of width 160, gated lexical injection |
+| Lexical table | 320,001,536 rows by 160 columns, 51.2B parameters |
+| Vision | 27 layers, width 1,152, 16-pixel patches, merger output width 2,560 |
+
+The residual state is `[T, 4 * D]`. Each sublayer reads `[T, D]` and writes its
+update into the four streams. PLE uses original token IDs and one-dimensional
+document positions, independently of multimodal rotary coordinates.
+
+QSA caches document/block/tail metadata once per input. Equal ReLU scores select
+earlier blocks first, so masked future tokens cannot change a past selection.
+HF uses an unspecified cutoff tie policy; reference comparisons use positive
+selection margins and report natural router/block choices separately.
+
+The architecture supplies no indexer training coefficient. `indexer_loss=None`
+disables the objective; test recipes explicitly select coefficient 1.0. The
+attention-teacher KL uses detached teacher and backbone inputs, so it trains
+only the indexer. MoE auxiliary counts exclude padded tokens.
+
+## Build and train
+
+```python
+from torchtitan.config.parallelism import ParallelismConfig
+from torchtitan.models.qwen3_8_flash_next import build_model_config
+
+parallelism = ParallelismConfig(data_parallel_shard_degree=2)
+model = build_model_config("debugmodel", parallelism=parallelism, seq_len=64)
+```
+
+Flavors are `debugmodel`, `debugmodel_mm`, and `125B-A6B`. Reduced fixtures retain
+both attention types, PLE, four residual streams, and routed/shared experts.
+This change supports FSDP. TP, EP, PP and CP are rejected explicitly.
+
+```bash
+NGPU=1 MODULE=torchtitan_recipes.tests.models.qwen3_8_flash_next \
+  CONFIG=qwen38_flash_next_debugmodel ./run_train.sh
+```
+
+## Numerical coverage
+
+| Path | Modes and checks | Reference |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Gated residual and norms | FP32/BF16 forward, input and parameter gradients | Independent equations and pinned HF |
+| Lexical embedding | Fresh hash initialization, EOS/packed resets, padding, lookup and convolution gradients | Independent hash/convolution equations |
+| QSA | Pruned block selection, causal tails, padding, exact ties, selected-attention backward | Chronological block oracle and selected-token SDPA |
+| Indexer teacher | Detached KL, indexer-only gradients, global token denominator | Independent differentiable KL |
+| Router | Natural expert sets, rounded-logit softmax, mixing weights, eager/compiled backward | FP32 softmax over BF16 logits |
+| Decoder | Train/eval logits, normalized CE, embedding input and all 184 mapped parameter gradients | Same-weight HF; 39 tokens, eight-layer fixture |
+| Vision | Packed images/video, merger, pixel and 41 parameter gradients | Same-weight HF vision |
+| Full multimodal model | Train/eval image/video fusion, MRoPE, masked CE, pixel and all 225 parameter gradients | Same-weight HF conditional generation |
+| Adapter | Strict roundtrip and all released key/shape mappings | Published checkpoint headers |

+"""Qwen Sparse Attention with complete-block selection and indexer distillation."""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import NamedTuple
+
+import spmd_types as spmd
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+import torch_remat as remat
+from torch.nn.attention import sdpa_kernel, SDPBackend
+
+from torchtitan.distributed.accelerator_graph import accelerator_graphs_supported
+from torchtitan.models.base.module import Module
+from torchtitan.models.common import Linear
+from torchtitan.models.common.attention import InnerAttention, local_head_split
+from torchtitan.models.common.aux_loss import AuxLoss
